unit-m3u7.title: Unit 3 · Lesson 7: Solve Problems with Multiplication
unit-m3u7.source: enVision Topic 3 textbook scan — Multiply Multi-Digit Whole Numbers (Drive)

summary.text: Lesson 3-7 of the Topic 3 textbook scan: using multiplication to solve real problems — bills, distances and totals — by estimating first and then computing.

why.text: This is where the multiplication she has learned turns into something useful: working out yearly costs, comparing prices and checking if something is enough.

objectives.text: Choose multiplication to solve real-world problems
Estimate before computing to check reasonableness
Tell how often a bill is paid: monthly, quarterly, weekly

parentNote.text: The trap worth watching is the one the textbook sets on purpose: quarterly versus monthly. A quarterly bill is paid 4 times a year, not 12, and several wrong options multiply by the wrong one. The other idea is grouping before multiplying — adding two quarterly bills first and multiplying once. The price comparison question is deliberately close ($3,723 against $3,710) so it cannot be settled by glancing at the price per trip.

nextUp.text: Name what the answer is counting, then multiply.

cards.def:
**Decide what the answer is counting before you pick numbers to multiply.**
• "Each", "per" and "times as many" usually mean multiply.
• Write the answer with its label: dollars, miles, pages.
cards.hint: Name the answer first, then find it.

cards.def:
**Monthly = 12 times a year. Quarterly = 4 times a year. Weekly = 52 times a year.**
• A $645 quarterly bill costs 645 × 4 = $2,580 a year.
cards.hint: Quarter = one fourth of a year.

cards.def:
**If several amounts all repeat the same number of times, add them first.**
• Two quarterly bills of $430 and $290: 4 × (430 + 290) = 4 × 720 = $2,880.
cards.hint: Add what repeats together, then multiply once.

cards.def:
**Estimate first so you know roughly what answer to expect.**
• 137 × 22 is about 140 × 20 = 2,800.
cards.hint: An estimate is your early-warning system.

cards.def:
**Multiplying bigger numbers uses the same steps — just more of them.**
• Ones row, tens row, add. Carry as you go.

questions.q: A bill is paid quarterly. How many times is it paid in a year?
steps: A quarterly bill is paid every quarter of a year.

ex.main: **4.** Quarterly means once every three months — four times a year.
ex.tip: Monthly is 12. Mixing the two is the commonest slip in bill problems.

questions.q: A water bill is $645, paid quarterly. What does water cost for the whole year?
questions.hint: How many quarters are in a year?
steps: It is paid 4 times a year.

ex.tip: $7,740 multiplies by 12 as if the bill were monthly.

questions.q: A phone plan costs $58 each month. How much is that in a year?

ex.tip: $232 multiplies by 4 — that would be a quarterly bill.

questions.q: Carlos saves 24 cents every day of a 365-day year. How many cents does he save?
questions.hint: Multiply cents per day by the number of days.

ex.tip: 2,190 leaves the zero off the tens row.

questions.q: Lila drives 137 kilometers round trip to work. How far does she drive in 22 work days?
questions.hint: Multiply the distance each day by the number of days.

questions.q: Which costs more: 14 trips at $265 each, or 17 trips at $219 each?
questions.hint: Work out both totals, then compare.

ex.tip: The price per trip alone is not enough — the number of trips changes the answer.

questions.q: A can of paint covers 300 square feet. A wall is 18 feet wide and 14 feet high. Is one can enough?
opts: Yes — 18 + 14 = 32, which is much less than 300
No — the wall is 252 square feet, which is more than 300
Yes — the wall is 252 square feet, which is less than 300
No — the wall is 2,520 square feet
questions.hint: The wall's area is width × height.
steps: 252 is less than 300, so one can is enough.

ex.main: **Yes.** The wall is 252 square feet, and one can covers 300.
ex.tip: Adding the sides gives the distance around, not the space to paint.

questions.q: A cook uses 125 pounds of potatoes each day for 14 days. How many pounds does she need?
questions.hint: Multiply pounds per day by the number of days.

questions.q: In 3_8 × 40 = 13,920, one digit is missing. Which digit is it?
questions.hint: Try each digit and check which product is 13,920.

ex.tip: Estimate first: 13,920 ÷ 40 is about 350, which points straight at 348.

questions.q: Two bills are paid quarterly: $430 for gas and $290 for water. What do they cost together for a year?
questions.hint: Add the two bills first, then multiply by the number of quarters.

ex.tip: $2,010 multiplies only the gas bill by 4. $8,640 multiplies by 12 as if monthly.
